S.Korea, Japan chip stocks slide; KOSPI entered trading halt

Heavyweight chipmakers Samsung Electronics (KS:005930) and SK Hynix Inc (KS:000660) slumped 5.5% and 8%, respectively.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng index jumped 3.5% with Chinese chipmaking stocks leading gains.

The Democratic victories in U.S. midterms raised expectations that political pressure could accelerate efforts to end the U.S.-Iran conflict, potentially easing supply disruptions and reducing inflationary pressures.
Lower energy prices also boosted bond markets as investors scaled back expectations of further Federal Reserve interest-rate increases.

title: Gold surges past $4,130 as US election sends dollar, Treasury yields tumbling
full_text:
Investing.com -- Gold prices extended their rally on Thursday, climbing above $4,130 an ounce as the Democratic election victory continued to weigh on the U.S. dollar and Treasury yields, boosting demand for the precious metal.
At 23:55 ET (04:55 GMT), spot gold surged 1.9% to $4,138.51 an ounce, while U.S. gold futures gained 1.8% to $4,147.59. Silver advanced 1.6% to $53.0750 an ounce, while platinum climbed 2% to $1,529.40. Spot palladium rose 2.3% to $1,030.54, while palladium futures gained 2.2% to $1,026.75. The U.S. dollar Index fell 0.3% to 101.27.
The Democratic election victory, which dealt a setback to the Trump administration, triggered a broad decline in U.S. bond yields and the dollar. Treasury yields fell across maturities on Wednesday and extended their retreat on Thursday, while the greenback lost 0.4% in the previous session before weakening further.
Lower yields support gold because it does not pay interest, while a softer dollar makes bullion more affordable for international buyers.
ANZ analysts said U.S. bonds also benefited from expectations that the new political balance would constrain Trump’s proposed tax cuts and spending plans.
However, they cautioned that government borrowing has been a significant source of support for gold over the past year, meaning restrictions on fiscal expansion could weaken one of the factors underpinning bullion’s longer-term appeal.
Oil prices remained sharply lower after Brent crude dropped below $100 a barrel on Wednesday for the first time since early October. Trump played down the possibility of renewed strikes against Iran following the election setback, helping ease fears of further escalation and energy supply disruptions.
Gold’s recovery marks its strongest break yet from a months-long decline, although the metal remains more than 20% below its levels before the U.S.-Iran war erupted in late February.
The conflict drove energy costs higher and fuelled inflation, prompting tighter monetary policy that weighed on non-yielding bullion.
Investors will now look to Friday’s U.S. nonfarm payrolls report for fresh evidence on economic conditions and the interest-rate outlook. Signs that inflation is moderating could give the Federal Reserve greater flexibility to ease monetary policy, potentially providing further support to gold.

title: NAB shares slump 7% to three-week low as FY26 cash earnings miss
full_text:
Investing.com -- National Australia Bank shares slumped on Thursday after the lender reported weaker full-year earnings, with higher credit impairment charges and software-related costs weighing on profitability.
Shares fell 7.5% to A$38.08, touching their lowest level since October 12 and sharply underperforming the broader S&P/ASX 200, which was up 1.8% in morning trading.
Cash earnings fell 13.4% to A$6.14 billion for the year ended September 30, missing the Visible Alpha consensus estimate of about A$6.33 billion. Statutory net profit attributable declined 9.1% to A$6.14 billion, below analysts' A$6.45 billion estimate.
Net operating income increased 5.8% to A$22.01 billion, supported by higher lending volumes and improved margins. However, credit impairment charges jumped 85.7% to A$1.55 billion from A$833 million a year earlier, including a A$403 million increase in collective provisions reflecting a more challenging economic outlook.
The bank's cash earnings included A$1.35 billion in large notable items, primarily related to a change in its software capitalisation policy. Excluding these items, cash earnings remained broadly flat at A$7.09 billion, also below analysts' A$7.24 billion estimate on an adjusted basis.
NAB's net interest margin (NIM) improved 6 basis points to 1.80%, as at quarter end.
The increase in credit charges included A$1.08 billion in individually assessed provisions, primarily related to business lending customers.
Business and Private Banking remained a source of strength, with cash earnings excluding large notable items increasing 10.7%. However, Corporate and Institutional Banking earnings fell 6.1%, while New Zealand Banking earnings declined 14%.
NAB said it expects underlying cost growth of less than 3% in FY27, while planning to maintain investment spending at a similar level to FY26, when it spent A$1.8 billion.
The bank had also announced plans to cut up to 2,500 roles by September 2027 as part of a broader restructuring programme, with the changes expected to generate about A$300 million in restructuring costs in 2027.
CEO Andrew Irvine warned that persistent inflation, higher interest rates and weaker housing conditions would weigh on the operating environment.
“The actions we've taken reflect our expectation of a tough year ahead,” he said.
NAB declared a final dividend of 85 Australian cents per share, fully franked, taking its total dividend for FY26 to A$1.70 per share, unchanged from the previous financial year.

title: Goldman flags fresh state buying in China stocks, awaits volume recovery
full_text:
Investing.com-- China’s stock market has received fresh support from state-backed investors, although a sustained recovery remains uncertain as trading activity and investor sentiment have yet to show convincing improvement, Goldman Sachs analysts said in a note.
Buying by China’s national team (NT) through exchange-traded funds began around mid-October and has accelerated in recent sessions, with cumulative inflows over the past two weeks surpassing the total recorded in April 2025, Goldman Sachs said.

title: Tencent shares jump 6% to three-week high after Hunyuan AI model launch
full_text:
Investing.com -- Tencent (HK:0700) shares surged to a three-week high on Thursday after the Chinese technology giant unveiled its latest Hunyuan artificial intelligence model, adding visual understanding and computer-use capabilities.
Shares rose 5.93% to HK$425.40, their highest level since October 16, outperforming the broader Hang Seng Index, which was up 3.3% at 11:12 a.m. Hong Kong time.
Tencent's Hunyuan team officially launched Hy4 on Wednesday, introducing visual understanding for the first time alongside improvements in instruction following, long-context comprehension and long-horizon agentic tasks.
The new model can process detailed images, analyse complex charts and perform mathematical visual reasoning. It also introduces computer-use capabilities, allowing it to interact with command-line and graphical interfaces to perform tasks across different applications.
Hy4 has been trained for professional software applications including Blender and computer-aided design (CAD), improving its ability to plan and execute complex tasks over extended periods.
The release marks another step in Tencent's efforts to strengthen its AI model development and integrate its technology more deeply into enterprise software and consumer-facing applications.
The Hy4 model has expanded its parameter scale to 770 billion, compared with fewer than 300 billion in the Hy3 series, according to Hong Kong media reports. Tencent said it plans to release the model weights and system cards in the coming days, extending its open-source AI strategy.
The model is also being integrated into Tencent's WorkBuddy and CodeBuddy productivity platforms, while its API is available through Tencent Cloud TokenHub. The company is keeping API pricing unchanged from the Hy4 preview version.
Tencent said it restricted Hy4's cybersecurity training to defensive applications, such as identifying and fixing software vulnerabilities, excluding material that could help users build hacking tools or break into systems.
The launch comes as Chinese technology companies accelerate development of generative AI models to compete with leading US developers. Tencent has been releasing major Hunyuan model updates approximately every two months since rebuilding its AI infrastructure in February, according to Caixin.

title: Australia’s 188-year-old retailer David Jones enters administration, faces sale
full_text:
By Renju Jose
SYDNEY, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Australia’s 188-year-old department store chain, David Jones, was placed into voluntary administration on Thursday, as rising costs, sluggish retail sales and supply chain pressures weighed on its business.
David Jones stores will continue to operate under the control of FTI Consulting, the appointed receivers, while the firm reviews current operations.
McGrathNicol has been appointed as voluntary administrators.
"A transaction process seeking offers for a recapitalisation of the business or a sale as a going concern will commence immediately, and will be managed by McGrathNicol," FTI Consulting and McGrathNicol said in a joint statement.
"We will manage this process carefully, mindful of the impact on some stakeholders but also recognising the need for difficult decisions."
Founded in Sydney in 1838 by Welsh immigrant David Jones, the upscale retailer describes itself as the world’s oldest continuously operating department store.
With about 6,000 employees across 38 stores in Australia and New Zealand, David Jones is one of Australia’s most recognisable brands and predates London’s Harrods by more than a decade.
For generations, Australian shoppers have turned to David Jones for clothing and accessories for milestone occasions, from formal wear to school and graduation attire.
However, like overseas counterparts, the retailer has struggled for more than a decade as the rise of online shopping and competition from fast-fashion chains have steadily eroded its traditional department store business model.
Its latest owner was private equity firm Anchorage Capital Partners, which bought it from South African retailer Woolworths in 2022 for a price media reported at the time was about A$100 million ($70.09 million).
David Jones CEO Erica Berchtold said the retailer had "a well-developed plan on how to reset the business for the future."
She added that the company would work with the administrators, receivers and its secured lender during the voluntary administration process, Australia’s closest equivalent to Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
Luxury US department store owner Saks Global, which battled similar retail trends, emerged from Chapter 11 in June after nearly five months with fewer than half of its previous stores and a quarter of its debt.
Scentre Group, which owns and operates Westfield shopping centres in Australia and New Zealand, offered a lifeline to David Jones, but it was rejected by Anchorage Capital, ABC News reported, citing Scentre CEO Elliott Rusanow.
David Jones has stores at 17 Westfield locations.
In a statement to the Australian Securities Exchange on Wednesday, Scentre said David Jones had paid rent up to September 30.
($1 = 1.4267 Australian dollars)

title: Japan services PMI grows for fifth straight month in October

The S&P Global final Japan Services PMI rose to 51.7 in October from 51.3 in September. The reading came in below the flash estimate of 52.0. A reading above 50 indicates expansion, while below 50 signals contraction.
New orders increased for the 28th consecutive month, with the growth rate accelerating from September. Companies reported stronger domestic demand, new clients and business development efforts as contributing factors.

Cost pressures continued to ease, with input price inflation slowing for the fourth straight month to an eight-month low. Output price inflation also moderated, though prices have risen every month for the past four and a half years.
Business confidence fell to its lowest level since March. Companies cited concerns over inflation, an aging population and labor shortages as factors that tempered optimism about growth in the defense and technology sectors, business expansion plans and increased tourism.
Japan’s composite PMI index declined to 52.1 from 52.3, representing the softest growth pace since May. Stronger growth in services activity was offset by a slowdown in manufacturing output.

title: Democrats vow to rein in Trump as he shows off White House ballroom
full_text:
By Gram Slattery, David Morgan and Jason Lange
WASHINGTON, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Democrats vowed to use their resounding midterm victory to rein in President Donald Trump, setting up two years of possible deadlock in Washington, as Trump spent his first post-election appearance showing off his under-construction White House ballroom.
A wave of anger over Trump’s policies, particularly the US-Iran war’s role in pushing the cost of living higher, helped Democrats take the Senate, where they flipped seats in deeply Republican states for a majority of at least 54-44. Democrats also gained at least 30 seats in the House of Representatives.
It will be the first time that Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress.
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Wednesday that the incoming majority would be focused on affordability and accountability.
"We don’t work for Donald Trump," Jeffries, a New York lawmaker who is on track to become the first Black speaker of the House, told reporters on Wednesday. "We work for the American people. And the days of the House of Representatives functioning like a wholly owned subsidiary of the Trump administration are over."
’FOR ME, IT’S RELAXING’
Trump, who had devoted his last pre-election public appearance on Monday to talking about his renovations of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, called in reporters on the morning after his party’s sweeping midterm defeat to show off the ballroom he is building at the White House.
"When I get criticized, like, ’Why are you working on the White House?’ I’m doing it because the White House is the ultimate symbol of America, and it’s got to be pristine, it’s got to be perfect," Trump said. "For me, it’s relaxing."
He turned only briefly to the elections during his nearly hour-long appearance, telling reporters, "I’ll get along probably with the Democrats, unless they want to be destructive, but I have the power of the veto."
Trump had cast the midterm elections as a referendum on the first half of his second four-year stint in the White House, repeatedly urging his Republican base to "pretend I’m on the ballot," a message that Democratic Party leaders were happy to amplify.
The result: voters in conservative strongholds who propelled the president to his second term in office just two years ago swung dramatically toward Democrats, fueled by deep frustration over the unpopular war with Iran, anxiety over the high cost of living and anger at Trump’s stewardship of the country.
In Texas, the biggest Republican-led state before Tuesday, Democrats ended a decades-long losing streak in seismic fashion, winning their first Senate seat there since 1988 and ousting three-term Governor Greg Abbott.
Kansas elected its first Democratic senator since the Great Depression nearly a century ago, and in South Carolina, a state that Trump carried by nearly 18 points in 2024, Democrats turned aside his hand-picked Senate candidate.
WAITING ON ALASKA, MISSISSIPPI
Extremely close Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi remained uncalled as of Wednesday, leaving open the possibility that the Democrats’ majority could increase by two more seats to 56-44.
The Alaska race may not be called for more than a week because of ranked-choice tabulation, while the timeline for a decision in Mississippi remained unclear.
Once seated in January, Democrats are expected to use their power to investigate Trump’s administration, family and allies and demand concessions on major legislation. The Democratic Senate can block Trump’s nominees, including any US Supreme Court justices should a vacancy arise.
The Democratic victory is fueling questions about the longevity of the Supreme Court’s two eldest justices, Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito, and the durability of its conservative majority.
In the meantime, Republicans hold the reins and will have at least one must-pass piece of legislation ahead – a measure to fund the federal government past December – that they could use to enact conservative priorities during the so-called lame-duck period.
The loss also upended Republicans’ House leadership, with House Speaker Mike Johnson saying he would not continue to lead his caucus next year.
Trump, who is barred by the US Constitution from seeking a third term, acknowledged the war with Iran had played a role in his party’s losses but stood by his decision.
Vice President JD Vance, who may run as a successor to Trump in the 2028 election, piled blame on his boss’s decision to attack Iran in February.
"The reason we lost is the war," Vance wrote in a long social media post. "The president himself said so last night. If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay."
’EXTINCTION-LEVEL EVENT’
Democrats focused their campaign on corruption and affordability, blaming Trump’s expensive tariffs on imports, some of which were ruled to be an illegal tax by the courts, and the war with Iran for driving up costs while highlighting the billions of dollars the Trump family has made since he returned to the White House.
Republicans, led by Trump, accused Democrats of being out of step with voters on transgender people’s rights and other social issues, portraying them as radical and extreme. Voters made it clear they were more concerned with pocketbook issues.
"This is close to an extinction-level event for Republicans," Republican Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said in public remarks analyzing the results.
The Democratic wave flooded huge swaths of the country. Republicans lost ground in 99% of the approximately 2,100 counties where most votes had been counted as of Wednesday morning, according to tallies compiled by Reuters and USA Today.

title: Nintendo first-half profit rises 11% as software sales offset weaker hardware
full_text:
Investing.com -- Nintendo reported higher first-half profit as strong software sales and a refund of U.S. tariffs helped lift operating earnings, offsetting lower hardware sales, while the Japanese videogame maker maintained its full-year financial forecast.
Profit attributable rose 11% to ¥220.92 billion for the six months ended September 30, compared with ¥198.94 billion a year earlier. Revenue fell 12.1% to ¥966.04 billion, while operating profit jumped 49.1% to ¥216.5 billion from ¥145.18 billion.
Nintendo said operating profit benefited from steady software sales, which accounted for a larger proportion of total revenue, as well as a first-quarter refund of U.S. tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act that had previously been recorded as cost of sales.
Nintendo Switch 2 hardware sales reached 6.49 million units during the first half, while software sales totalled 24.49 million units. Sales of the original Nintendo Switch hardware reached 1.27 million units, while software sales totalled 65.73 million units. Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream and Rhythm Heaven Groove sold 8.81 million and 2.89 million units, respectively.
Digital sales increased 60.5% to ¥249.6 billion, mainly reflecting higher sales of downloadable versions of packaged software. Revenue from intellectual property-related businesses climbed 87.9% to ¥62.7 billion, supported by strong audience engagement with The Super Mario Galaxy Movie.
Nintendo left its full-year financial forecast unchanged, expecting revenue of ¥2.05 trillion for the year ending March 2027, down 11.4% from the previous year. Operating profit is forecast at ¥370 billion, up 2.7%, while ordinary profit is expected to fall 20.7% to ¥430 billion. Profit attributable is projected to decline 26.9% to ¥310 billion.
The company set an interim dividend of ¥76 per share and forecast a year-end payout of ¥86, bringing its expected annual dividend to ¥162 per share, compared with ¥219 in the previous financial year.
Nintendo said it aims to expand the installed base of Switch 2 by increasing sales of existing titles and continuing to introduce new games. Upcoming releases include The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and Metroid Ravenous.

title: China says US farm purchases hinge on tariff-cut deal
full_text:
BEIJING, Nov 5 (Reuters) - China is open to buying US farm goods, but only on the condition that the two sides reach an agreement on reciprocal tariff cuts, the commerce ministry said on Thursday.
Following a September summit between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump in Washington, the two sides proposed a $60 billion package of reciprocal tariff cuts, including roughly $17 billion worth of US farm goods that China imported in 2024, though the plan has yet to be finalised.
"China hopes the United States will work with China to create favourable conditions for agricultural trade between the two countries through measures such as jointly lowering tariffs, reducing non-tariff barriers and expanding market access," said Huang Ling, a commerce ministry spokesperson, during a regular press briefing.
The White House said in May that Beijing had agreed to buy $17 billion of US agricultural goods annually from 2026, with this year’s target adjusted on a prorated basis.
Those purchases were in addition to a commitment made in October last year to buy US soybeans.
China is on track to meet its soybean purchase target, but bought only $7.2 billion of other US agricultural products, including meat and corn, between January and September, according to a Reuters analysis.
Uncertainty persists over when the clock starts on the $17 billion non-soy purchase deal, as the White House has not said whether the timeline began with its May announcement or will begin only once China’s proposed tariff cuts are finalised.
Imports of those products were at their lowest level for the period since 2019, at the height of the first US-China trade war.
The slow pace of buying has fuelled doubts over whether imports will rise sharply this year, adding to pressure on US farmers already grappling with high fuel costs.
Traders have told Reuters that lower tariffs would be needed to make large-scale purchases commercially viable.

title: ArcelorMittal beats third quarter estimates on higher margins
full_text:
Investing.com -- ArcelorMittal SA (AS:MT) on Thursday reported third quarter results that exceeded analyst expectations, with EBITDA of $2.0 billion beating the consensus estimate of $1.97 billion by 3%.
The world’s leading integrated steel and mining company posted adjusted earnings per share of $1.15, surpassing the $0.84 consensus estimate. EBITDA increased 34% YoY to $2.0 billion, with EBITDA per tonne improving to $155, up $44 per tonne compared to the prior year period.
The company reported an adjusted net income of $0.9 billion in the third quarter, compared with $0.7 billion in the second quarter. However, ArcelorMittal recorded a reported net loss of $0.4 billion, which included impairment and exceptional items related to the idling of ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih in Ukraine.
Revenue performance benefited from strategic growth investments, optimized assets and diversified market exposures. The company expects fourth quarter flat shipment growth to accelerate with a double-digit YoY increase, and Group shipments in the second half of 2026 to exceed those in the first half.
"Enhanced EU trade measures are beginning to rebalance European steel market fundamentals, reducing import penetration and supporting higher domestic capacity utilization," the company stated. Following implementation of new tariff rate quotas, ArcelorMittal has brought all its European blast furnaces back into operation.
Net debt increased to $10.3 billion as of September 30, 2026, reflecting $0.4 billion of shareholder returns and a temporary $0.5 billion net working capital investment during the quarter. The company generated $0.5 billion of underlying free cash flow in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, after investing $1.1 billion in strategic growth projects.
ArcelorMittal returned $1.1 billion to shareholders through dividends and share buybacks during the first nine months of 2026. The company maintained its 2026 capital expenditure guidance at $4.5 billion to $5.0 billion, including $1.7 billion to $1.9 billion of strategic capex. The portfolio of organic growth projects and completed M&A is expected to increase EBITDA potential by approximately $1.8 billion from 2026 and beyond.

title: UK inflation to peak at 4.4% around start of 2027, FT survey shows
full_text:
Investing.com -- British inflation is set to peak at an average 4.4% around the start of 2027, well above official forecasts, a Financial Times survey of economists showed, hours before the Bank of England is expected to raise interest rates.
The survey of 12 economists was conducted this week, the FT reported on Thursday. Most expect price growth to reach its highest level in the first quarter of 2027. All but one expect a peak above 4.1%, and five forecast a peak of between 4.5% and 5%.
The Bank of England will set out its own inflation and growth outlook at midday on Thursday after a meeting widely expected to agree a quarter-point rise in its key interest rate.
The economists’ forecasts are higher than the Office for Budget Responsibility’s projection, published last week, of a 3.8% peak in the first quarter of next year.
The OBR based its forecasts on oil and gas prices from mid-August, before a re-escalation in the Middle East war pushed them sharply higher.
The OBR said its inflation forecast for early 2027 would have been "somewhat higher" at current market prices. Oil prices fell on Wednesday after a report of diplomatic progress between the United States and Iran.
Ofgem’s energy price cap is on track to rise by over 25% in January, and household energy bills are set to jump by nearly £470 to about £2,200 a year for a typical household, according to EDF Energy’s estimates.
Inflation was 3.5% in September, its highest in almost a year. A 4.4% reading would be the fastest since October 2023, when it hit 4.6%.
The most common forecast among them for the BoE’s benchmark rate peak is 4.25%, which implies two quarter-point increases. Traders are fully pricing in four quarter-point increases by the end of next year.

title: Ambu shares jump 6% on strong Q4 growth, upbeat guidance
full_text:
Investing.com -- Ambu A/S reported fourth-quarter revenue of DKK 1,700 million, up 13.9% on an organic basis and 16% on a reported basis from DKK 1,466 million in the prior year period.
Shares of the medical device company climbed 6% following the release of results and guidance for fiscal 2026/27.
The company projects organic revenue growth of 9.5% to 11.5% and an EBIT margin of 13% to 15% for the new fiscal year. Ambu expects its Endoscopy Solutions segment to deliver approximately 15% organic growth.
The Endoscopy Solutions segment posted 21.2% organic growth in the fourth quarter.
Respiratory grew 21% organically, supported by the launch of SureSight Mobile. Urology, ENT & GI increased 21.3% organically.
Anesthesia & Patient Monitoring recorded 2.8% organic growth, with Patient Monitoring up 6.5% and Anesthesia down 0.6%.
North America grew 17.9%, driven by Endoscopy Solutions. Europe posted 8.5% growth and Rest of World increased 15.1%.
Fourth-quarter EBIT reached DKK 293 million, producing a 17.2% margin compared to DKK 147 million and a 10% margin in the prior-year period.
The improvement reflected operating leverage and a positive effect from tariff reclaims, partially offset by commercial organization investments.
"We ended the year with strong momentum, delivering 13.9% organic revenue growth in Q4, driven by 21.2% organic growth in Endoscopy Solutions," said Chief Executive Officer Britt Meelby Jensen.
Free cash flow before acquisitions totaled DKK 216 million, up from DKK 130 million in the prior-year quarter. Ambu plans to return DKK 551 million to shareholders in 2026/27 through a proposed DKK 151 million dividend and a DKK 400 million share buyback program.

title: Rheinmetall shares slide as investors question growth outlook after second guidance cut
full_text:
By Maria Rugamer
Nov 5 (Reuters) - Rheinmetall shares fell 13% on Thursday, the biggest decline in the STOXX 600, after the German defence group cut its outlook for a second time in three months, fuelling concerns about its ability to deliver on growth targets tied to Europe’s rearmament drive.
The company cut its 2026 sales forecast to about €13.2 billion ($14.9 billion) from a previous range of €13.7 billion to 14.2 billion and lowered its operating margin target to about 18.5% from around 19%.
The company said revenue and advance payments linked to Germany’s Arminius Boxer vehicle programme would move into next year and that slower batch approvals would delay artillery ammunition revenue. It also said not all expected revenue from newer activities, including cooperation with Dutch missile maker Destinus, would materialise in 2026.
Chief Executive Armin Papperger said in August that Rheinmetall’s share of an initial Arminius order could amount to about €12.4 billion and that the company expected an advance payment worth more than €3 billion.
EXECUTION QUESTIONS EMERGE
While Rheinmetall blamed the downgrade on the delayed Arminius award and ammunition approval bottlenecks, investors appeared focused on broader concerns around execution and cash generation.
Order intake totalled €2.89 billion in the third quarter, below sales of €3.15 billion, while operating free cash flow was negative €82 million. Rheinmetall also dropped its target for a cash conversion rate above 40%.
"The Boxer contract seems not to be the whole story," a local trader said, pointing to weak order intake, negative free cash flow and the lack of revised backlog guidance.
Analysts at Jefferies said they were surprised by the size of the outlook cut so late in the year and noted Rheinmetall had yet to provide revised order guidance despite the Arminius delay.
The selloff came despite a strong quarter in which sales rose to €3.15 billion from €2.31 billion a year earlier and operating profit increased 62% to €553 million.
Rheinmetall’s order book remains among the largest in the European defence sector and demand from rearming European governments remains strong. The latest warning instead raised questions over how quickly the company can convert that demand into revenue, cash flow and programme deliveries.

title: GN Store Nord soars 16% on stronger-than-expected Q3 print
full_text:
DENMARK - GN Store Nord (CSE:GN) reported third-quarter results that exceeded analyst expectations, with shares surging 16%.
The company posted organic sales growth of approximately 2%, slightly ahead of the 1.8% analyst consensus. Divisional profit margin reached 34.4%, significantly above the 27.8% consensus estimate.
Excluding a tariff refund, the margin was 27.7%, still well above expectations. The strong margin performance reflected gross margin improvements in gaming and a DKK153 million tariff refund booked in the quarter.
Adjusted EBITA including tariff refund reached DKK413 million versus the DKK248 million consensus, translating to an 18.2% margin and a 940 basis point YoY expansion.
Excluding the tariff refund, adjusted EBITA was DKK260 million compared to the DKK179 million consensus, representing an 11.5% margin and a 270 basis point YoY improvement.
GN reiterated its fiscal 2026 outlook, expecting 0-3% organic sales growth with a consensus of 0.6%. The Enterprise division is projected to deliver growth in the lower half of the -3% to 3% range, with a consensus of -1.8%, as EMEA market pressures continue but are expected to soften in the second half of 2026.
The Gaming division is anticipated to achieve growth in the lower half of the 7-13% range versus a 6.9% consensus, supported by market share gains despite muted consumer sentiment.
The company maintained its adjusted EBITA margin guidance of 9-10% for fiscal 2026, compared to the 9.0% consensus.
The discontinued Hearing division delivered 5% organic sales growth, exceeding the 2.7% consensus, driven by broad-based growth across regions and channels supported by the ReSound Sensia product.
